name: heartwork coffee
notes: Shopify /products.json is retail-only (6 bagged coffees), no in-house menu page or nav link found on heartworkcoffeebar.com. Fell back to tier-5: DoorDash's SEO store page (schema.org Menu JSON-LD, server-rendered, read via navigation headers) and allmenus (Grubhub) agree to the cent on all 23 items - independent owners (DoorDash vs Grubhub), so treated as two agreeing tier-5 sources per the ladder. allmenus carried 2 extra ambiguous duplicate rows (a second 'Iced Latte' $4.00 and a 'Hot Latte' $4.00 layered under a 'Not Coffee' section alongside the sized Espresso-section variants) that DoorDash's cleaner listing omits; dropped as scrape-duplication noise, not read as disagreement. Cents cluster on .00/.25/.50/.75 - no delivery-fee divisor (1.04/1.1/1.15/1.2/1.25) produces a round-number pattern, so no markup suspected. Price level (small counter, $2.50 double espresso, $4.50 small latte) is plausible for a walk-up-window cafe with no seating area, per its own Yelp reviews describing it as 'basically a pickup window.' Could not reach a dine-in artefact (no browser) to confirm currency further within budget.

name: Hungry Lu's
notes: hungrylus.com is a Canva-exported landing page with an 'Our Menu' heading but no item list or prices in the markup (image-only presentation, no nav link to an order page) - only outbound links found on it were to unrelated business sites (grabngosubs.com, mimmos.biz, montelepreforno.com), not menus. Fell back to DoorDash's marketplace store page (schema.org Menu JSON-LD, read via navigation headers), address confirmed as 4920 Voltaire Street matching the work list. Cents run .00/.29/.45/.49/.50/.99/.99 with no divisor (1.04-1.3) producing a round-number pattern, so no marketplace fee suspected - looks like the restaurant's own numbered sandwich board (items are literally numbered 1-18). Dropped one row, 'OB Special' ($50.00 personal 8in pizza) as an implausible outlier next to four sibling pizzas at $5.00-$6.45 - almost certainly an upstream data error, not a real price; did not invent a replacement. No second priced source reached to cross-check within budget.

name: Iron Door
notes: Remote desert dive bar in Ocotillo Wells/Borrego Springs (5460 Split Mountain Rd, matches work list). theirondoorbar.com is a bare Wix landing page with no menu section or nav link. Web search plus restaurantguru, wanderlog, mindtrip, restaurantji and place-all all describe it only as 'cold beer, pool table, complimentary popcorn, pepperoni pizza made on-site, weekend tacos/waffles specials' with an aggregate '$10-$20 per person' Yelp-style price band - none carry a single itemized dish price. No DoorDash/UberEats/Grubhub/order.online listing found, no Toast/Square/Clover storefront, no PDF or photographed board reachable without a browser. Treating as not-found: a simple dive-bar menu with no per-item prices published anywhere, matching the archetype in the playbook.

name: Feast and Fareway
notes: The bare www root is an unconfigured WordPress template ('Click to assign menu', placeholder Amsterdam address) - the real site lives one path deeper at /restaurant/. Its 'Menus' section embeds four full-page designed menu images (Brunch, Fareway Bar drinks, Kids' Menu, Snack Shack), fetched via the wp-json media endpoint at full resolution and read directly - a first-party, dated (uploads/2026/05, 2026/06, 2026/08) dine-in artefact, the strongest tier available. All four read cleanly with no ambiguous prices. Section list checked against DoorDash's own listing (which described fish tacos/nachos/burgers/salads under generic 'entrees') - those items are not on the current site menus at all; DoorDash's cached prices also divide cleanly by 1.15 onto round dollars ($18.40->$16, $9.20->$8, $16.10->$14, $20.70->$18, $17.25->$15), so that DoorDash listing is treated as stale/fee-marked and NOT used - the restaurant's own current photographed menus are the sole source here. Brunch runs 7:00am-3:00pm; Snack Shack (deli sandwiches, hot dogs, beer, snacks) appears to cover the rest of the day for the golf course. Kids' 'Hole-in-One' breakfast item is time-gated 7am-3pm, included as printed. Modifier add-ons ('+2' bacon, '+2.25' avocado, '+$2' chicken) are not separate dishes and were dropped, as were the two happy-hour discount blocks (not itemized dish prices). Sausage side lists two flavors at one price - both included at $6.00. Six-Pack Special carries two prices (import/domestic) - both included as separate rows.

notes: thefunkylemonsd.com sits behind a SiteGround bot-mitigation captcha wall (HTTP 202, redirect to /.well-known/sgcaptcha/) on every attempt with and without navigation headers - not bypassed, blocked and moved to the restaurant's own Toast storefront instead. __OO_STATE__ parsed by brace-balancing carried the full 11-group, 135-item catalog server-side (no client fetch needed). Cents run .00/.19/.25/.50/.75/.95/.99 - no delivery-fee divisor (1.04-1.3) produces a round-number cluster, so no markup suspected; this reads as the shop's own printed pricing. Dropped 2 items with a null price (Cup of Milk, Cup of Water - no real price to report) and dropped the pure retail-merchandise rows inside the 'MISC' group (apparel, tote bags, mugs, candles, palo santo/sage/incense, a meditation deck, coffee bean bags) as adjuncts; kept the grab-and-go bottled drinks that were mixed into the same group (water, kombucha, sodas, sparkling waters) as menu items, filed under 'Misc / Grab-and-Go Drinks'.

name: Hanaya Sushi
notes: hanayasushicafego.site (the work-list domain) still connect-times-out on retry, confirming the router's fetch-failed finding - genuinely dead, not a transient block. The JSON-LD on that page names a second domain, teamsina.com, which is a bare Squarespace 'under construction' parking page - also dead. SinglePlatform's own listing (address 10066 Pacific Heights Blvd, San Diego CA 92121 - exact match) was the only reachable source with real prices, read directly from its embedded schema.org OfferCatalog via plain curl. Only one priced source was reachable, so per the ladder this stands alone at medium confidence - flagging the known staleness risk explicitly rather than treating the read as current. Cents are almost entirely .95 with a few .00/.50 - a conventional printed-menu pattern, no delivery-fee divisor pattern found. Dropped the entire 'Bento' section (10 items) - every single price field was an empty string, matching the playbook's documented SinglePlatform failure mode of stripping prices server-side while keeping the item list; wrote no invented prices for it. Dropped 'Party Tray' ($30 catering tray) as a non-core adjunct. Kept Appetizer & Side, Deluxe Spicy Roll, Sushi (per-piece), and Rolls sections in full.
